q-35927.name: Question 1
q-35927.problem: Given the elliptic paraboloid $z+4=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{4}$, find its intercepts with the $x$-axis.
q-35927.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the paraboloid, we substitute $y=0$ and $z=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+4 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(0-4)^{2}}{4} \\ 4 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{16}{4} \\ 4 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+4 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the solution $x=0$

Therefore, the intercept with the $x$-axis is $(0,0,0)$ only.

q-164265.name: Question 2
q-164265.problem: Find the vertex of the elliptic paraboloid $3z+6=3(x-3)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}.$
q-164265.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic paraboloid oriented along the $z$-axis with vertex at a point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

To find the vertex, we rewrite our equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3z+6 & =3(x-3)^{2}+(y+2)^{2} \\ 3(z+2) & =3(x-3)^{2}+(y+2)^{2} \\ z+2 & =(x-3)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(y+2)^{2} \\ z-(-2) & =(x-3)^{2}+\frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic paraboloid that has its vertex at $(3,-2,-2).$

First, we write our equation as 

$$
x-0=\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(z-(-1))^{2}}{6}.
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic paraboloid oriented along the $x$-axis that has its vertex at $(0,3,-1).$
 Since it is oriented along the $x$-axis, we conclude that its axis of symmetry is parallel to the $x$-axis.

The axis of symmetry should pass through the vertex of the paraboloid. Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry can be written as an intersection of two planes:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=3 \\ z=-1\end{aligned}

q-72305.problem: Given the hyperbolic paraboloid $(x+3)^{2}-2(y-3)^{2}=z-2$, find its intercepts with the $x$-axis.

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)^{2}-2(0-3)^{2} & =0-2 \\ (x+3)^{2}-18 & =-2 \\ (x+3)^{2} & =16 \\ x+3 & =\pm 4 \\ x & =-3\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the solutions $x=-7$ and $x=1.$

Therefore, the intercepts with the $x$-axis are $(-7,0,0)$ and $(1,0,0).$

q-72303.problem: Find the saddle point of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z-5=5(x-1)^{2}-3(y+4)^{2}.$
q-72303.worked_solution:
The general equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

What is the trace in the yz-plane of the hyperbolic paraboloid z−3=(x−5)25−y24?

a
A hyperbola: 4x2−y2=1
b
A parabola: y2=4(z−3)
c
Two intersecting lines: y=±4(x−3)
d
Two parallel lines: y=4(x±5)
e
A parabola: y2=−4(z−8)
Submit

z−3=(0−5)25−y24z−3=255−y24z−3=5−y24z−8=−y24y2=−4(z−8)

q-164279.name: Question 12
q-164279.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z+2=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{3}?$
q-164279.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+2 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(0+3)^{2}}{3} \\ z+2 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{9}{3} \\ z+2 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-3 \\ z+5 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =2(z+5)\end{aligned}
$$

 

This gives us the equation of the parabola in $xz$-plane.

q-35931.name: Question 13
q-35931.problem: What is the trace in the $yz$-plane of the elliptic paraboloid $z+1=\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{3}.$
q-35931.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $yz$-plane, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+1 & =\frac{(0-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{3} \\ z+1 & =\frac{4}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{3} \\ z+1 & =1+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{3} \\ z & =\frac{1}{3}(y-1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This gives us the equation of the parabola in $yz$-plane.

Question 13

What is the trace in the yz-plane of the elliptic paraboloid z+1=(x−2)24+(y−1)23.

a
A parabola: z=13(y−1)2
b
Two intersecting lines: y=±(x−1)
c
A hyperbola: x2−3(y−1)2=1
d
A parabola: z=3(y−1)2
e
Two parallel lines: y=(z±3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the trace in the yz-plane, we substitute x=0 into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

z+1=(0−2)24+(y−1)23z+1=44+(y−1)23z+1=1+(y−1)23z=13(y−1)2

This gives us the equation of the parabola in yz-plane.

q-35517.name: Question 14
q-35517.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the elliptic paraboloid $z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{8}?$
q-35517.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(0+1)^{2}}{8} \\ z & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{8} \\ z-\frac{1}{8} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4} \\ {x}^{2} & =4z-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This gives us the equation of the parabola in $xz$-plane.

To find the trace in the xz-plane, we substitute y=0 into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

z−1=x24+022z−1=x24z=x24+1
